speaker: Sheldon
text: Mommy? Great news. My mom sent me my old Nintendo 64. You know what this means, don't you? Break out the Red Bull, it's time to rock Mario old school.

speaker: Leonard
text: Terrific. I kind of have other plans tonight.

speaker: Sheldon
text: But it's Friday. Friday's always vintage game night. Mom included the memory card. We can pick up right where I left off in 1999 when I had pernicious anemia.

speaker: Leonard
text: Well, the thing is, someone's coming over.

speaker: Sheldon
text: No problem. I have three controllers. The more the merrier.

speaker: Leonard
text: Sheldon, it's a date. I have a date coming over.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Oh. Well, you can't blame me for not jumping to that conclusion.

speaker: Leonard
text: Hi, what's so unusual about me having a date?

speaker: Leonard
text: Well, but nevertheless, I have one now, and I'd appreciate it if you would, you know, make yourself scarce.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Leonard, I am a published theoretical physicist with two doctors and an IQ which can't be accurately measured by normal tests. How much scarcer could I be?

speaker: Leonard
text: You know what I mean. Could you just give us a little privacy?

speaker: Sheldon
text: You want me to leave the apartment? You mean just go someplace else and be... someplace else? Well, why should I leave? This is my apartment, too.

speaker: Leonard
text: I know it is, and if science ever discovers a second member of your species and you two would like some privacy, I'd be more than happy to get out of your doorway.
